info.title: TourRadar Partner API
info.description:
# Overview

Welcome to the TourRadar Partner API documentation!

The TourRadar Partner API comprises a set of endpoints that can connect any partner to TourRadar’s global network of operators, providing the ability to search, view, and book adventures. You can use TourRadar's entire inventory or only the operators with whom you have direct commercial agreements.

The API provides a simple and modern REST interface to facilitate the integration work.

> **⚠ Please note:** the work on the API and the integration is still in progress. As the integration work continues, this documentation will be updated as well.

## Who is the API for?

The current iteration of the API is designed to be used by various types of partners who signed up with TourRadar, partners like OTAs, GDSs, travel content providers, travel agencies, B2B marketplaces.

If you want to sign up with TourRadar, you can use the following **[link](https://www.tourradar.com/distribution-api)**.

## Typical use cases of the TourRadar Partner API

The TourRadar Partner API can be used to carry out the following tasks:

### Search for tours

The **[search endpoint](#tag/Tours/paths/~1v1~1tours~1search/get)** will provide you with the functionality to replicate the filters on the **[TourRadar platform](https://www.tourradar.com/)** and find the right adventure. For an example of the search capabilities, you can look at the filters on the following [page](https://www.tourradar.com/d/europe).

### Get tour details

To get more information about a tour, you can use the **[tour detail endpoint](#tag/Tours/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}/get)** – it will return the high-level information with topics like itinerary, what's included and country-specific information.

### Get pricing details and calculate the price

You can use the **[prices endpoint](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures~1{departureId}~1price/post)** to get more information about the price of a specific departure date but also to understand any other optional extras(e.g. excursions) or accommodations.

### Departures and availability

**[Departures endpoint](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures/get)** retrieves all available departure dates for the specified tour. Every item will contain: departure date, departure type, guide languages offered and the price breakdown. A departure date can be one of the following types: guaranteed, scheduled and request.

### Create booking

You can create a booking by using the **[bookings endpoint](#tag/Bookings/paths/~1v1~1bookings/post)** and adding all the required entities to the request.

### Check booking status

Some bookings are not automatically confirmed, some are canceled afterwards or declined – so it's useful to retrieve the **[status of a booking](#tag/Bookings/paths/~1v1~1bookings~1{bookingId}~1status/get)**.

### Download bulk data

There are 2 endpoints that can be used to synchronize content and other data in a “bulk” way:
**[all tours from an operator](#tag/Bulk/paths/~1v1~1operators~1{operator}~1bulk~1tours/get)** and **[all the available departure dates for all tours from a single tour operator](#tag/Bulk/paths/~1v1~1operators~1{operator}~1bulk~1departures/get)**.

This data can be downloaded and then imported into the partner’s own database or system. While we recommend updating the departures and availability daily - the tour content can be cached for a longer time (for example, one week).


### Booking Retrieval (Fetch)

Agents can use the booking endpoint to retrieve (Fetch) detailed information about bookings directly created on the operator systems. Based on a set of request parameters, the API allows for retrieval of bookings from all operators in the scope of the project, using a uniform request/response schema that is largely based on the Open Travel Alliance standard (OTA).

## Rate limits

A rate limit is a restriction that an API imposes on the number of times a user or client can access the server within a specified period of time. Rate limits are introduced to protect the system from receiving more data than it can handle.

Our API has a rate limit of **10 requests per second**, exceeding this limit will return an error `429 Too Many Requests`.

## POST /oauth2/token
The /oauth2/token endpoint only supports HTTPS POST. The partners app client makes requests to this endpoint directly and not through the system browser.

For more information on the specification see [Token Endpoint](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#TokenEndpoint).

### Request Parameters in Header
#### Authorization
If the client was issued a secret, the client must pass its client_id and client_secret in the authorization header through [Basic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basic_access_authentication#Client_side) HTTP authorization. The secret is Basic Base64Encode(client_id:client_secret).

#### Content-Type
Must always be `'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'`.


### Request Parameters in Body

#### grant_type
Required. Grant type. Must be `client_credentials`.

#### scope
Optional. You can specify a list of scopes (permissions) associated to the authentication token. If not specified, all available permissions will be assigned.

You should use the `scope` parameter only to restrict permissions for specific usage. If multiple scopes are needed, these must be separated by space.

### Exchanging Client Credentials for an Access Token
- ClientId:  `7817mgzzf3idtkfekag69udlhr`
- App Client Secret: `5sg3g3fsase0hlqipp5tv077d5f52g1hh2s7rsvo8hgkdvg`
- Authorization code: ` Base64Encode(client_id:client_secret)` = `NzgxN21nenpmM2lkdGtmZWthZzY5dWRsaHI6NXNnM2czZnNhc2UwaGxxaXBwNXR2MDc3ZDVmNTJnMWhoMnM3cnN2bzhoZ2tkdmc=`

> **⚠ Please note:** all the above client credentials are just examples. If you do not know the client credentials for your account, please reach out to us and we will share these details with you.

#### Sample Request

```
POST https://oauth.api.sandbox.b2b.tourradar.com/oauth2/token >
Content-Type='application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
Authorization=Basic NzgxN21nenpmM2lkdGtmZWthZzY5dWRsaHI6NXNnM2czZnNhc2UwaGxxaXBwNXR2MDc3ZDVmNTJnMWhoMnM3cnN2bzhoZ2tkdmc=
grant_type=client_credentials
```

#### Sample response

```json
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json

{
    access_token: "eyJraWQiOiJCdHhZVUR4d0k......l4xXhV40gBH6vxvBg"
}
```

> **⚠ Please note:** you are responsible and should take every possible attention to not make your credentials known to anybody else. In particular, if you're developing a website, credentials should not be used in the front-end code of your application. As a general rule, not having hard-coded credentials in the application code is a good practice.

tags.name: Versioning
tags.description:
In order to ensure compatibility and consistence of the implemented software with the future development of this API, all endpoints are prefixed with a **version identifier** path component.

The current version identifier is `v1`. When breaking changes are introduced in an endpoint, a new iteration of that specific endpoint will be created with increased identifier (`v2`, `v3`, etc.), while the existing one will continue working with unchanged request, and response, definition and behaviour.

#### Deprecation Strategy

The previous version of an API endpoint will be marked as deprecated, and ultimately sunset, over a specified period of time, usually 12 months (unless special business or security requirements demand a different strategy).

#### Example

All requests to the endpoints present in this documentation will be composed of:

* base URL
* version identifier
* endpoint path

For example, to access the `/bookings/operator/{operator}/{bookingCode}` endpoint in the sandbox environment, the request will be:

* base URL: `https://api.sandbox.b2b.tourradar.com`
* version identifier: `v1`
* endpoint path: `/bookings/operator/{operator}/{bookingCode}`

Resulting example request path:

```
GET https://api.sandbox.b2b.tourradar.com/v1/bookings/operator/406/IVSYDS-A339296
```
#### Production URLs

Once you are ready to go live, please use the following production URLs:

* API base URL: `https://api.b2b.tourradar.com`
* OAuth URL: `https://oauth.api.sandbox.b2b.tourradar.com/oauth2/token`

get.description:
Returns a list of all the bookings created in the TourRadar system by your partner account.

#### Response formats

You can set the `Accept` header to define the response format you need.
The available values are:
- `application/json` (default). It will return an array of **BookingSearch** objects;

- `text/csv`, if this format is requested the `limit` query parameter is ignored. It will contain these fields:

| field         | type    | notes |
| ---------------   | ------- | ----- |
| booking_id        | integer | Unique identifier of the booking in the TourRadar system. |
| tour_id           | integer | Unique identifier for the tour in the TourRadar system. |
| tour_name         | string  | Name of the tour. |
| operator_id       | integer | Unique identifier for the tour operator in the TourRadar system.  |
| operator_name     | string  | Name of the tour operator. |
| tour_length_days  | integer | Length of the tour, expressed in number of days. |
| passengers        | integer | Number of passengers. |
| departure_date    | string  | Departure date that was booked, in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| return_date       | string  | Return date that was booked, in the format `YYYY-MM-DD`. |
| created_at        | string  | Exact timestamp of when the booking was created, in the ISO 8601 format. |
| confirmed_at      | string  | Exact timestamp of when the booking was confirmed, in the ISO 8601 format. Empty if it is not confirmed. |
| hold_expire_at    | string  | Exact timestamp of when the the hold will expire, in the ISO 8601 format. |
| type              | string  | Type of this booking record. Expected values: `booking`, `question`, `hold`. |
| status            | string  | Status of the booking. Expected values: `open_question`, `open_hold`, `pending`, `confirmed`, `declined`, `cancelled`, `hold_expired`, `hold_declined` |
| currency          | string  | Currency of the booking. |
| total_value       | number  | Total amount of the booking. |

post.description:
Creates a booking in the TourRadar system.

The payload must be sent as JSON in the request body.
The required entries are:

* `departure_id`: this is the unique identifier of the wanted departure date for the desired tour. To retrieve departure dates, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/departures](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures/get)** endpoint.
* `currency`: the currency that will be used for payments.
* `passengers`: the list of passengers in the booking.
* `email`: email used for communications regarding the booking (partner support email). Please be aware that this email is different than the one from passengers definition.

Furthermore, it's possible to add the following sections, if needed:

* `accommodations`: defines the desired accommodation types (if the tour offers them), and which passengers will use them.
* `optional_extras`: optional extra items that can be booked together with the tour.

This is an example of how the payload for a booking looks like:

```json
{
  "departure_id": 123,
  "currency": "EUR",
  "email": "dummy@mail.org",
  "passengers": [
    {
      "pax_number": 1,
      "price_category_id": 1,
      "fields" : {
        "first_name": "John",
        "last_name": "Doe",
        "email": "dummy@mail.org",
        "phone_number": "+431245678853",
        "date_of_birth": "21/05/2019",
        "nationality": "Germany",
        "gender": "male"
      }
    },
    {
      "pax_number": 2,
      "price_category_id": 2,
      "fields" : {
        "first_name": "John",
        "last_name": "Doe",
        "email": "dummy@mail.org",
        "phone_number": "+431245678853",
        "date_of_birth": "21/05/2019",
        "nationality": "Germany",
        "gender": "female"
      }
    }
  ],
  "accommodations": [
    {
      "id": 345,
      "passengers": [1, 2]
    }
  ],
  "optional_extras": [
    {
      "id": 456,
      "passengers": [2]
    }
  ],
}
```

#### Passengers definition

For each entry in the `passengers` array, these are the required fields:

* `pax_number`: this is the index of the passenger, starting with 1. The passenger number will be used in the accommodation and extras sections of the request, to assign specific passengers to elements of the booking.
* `price_category_id`: this defines the category of the passenger. To retrieve price categories, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/prices](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1prices/get)** endpoint.
* `fields`: this is the passenger information, as requested by the operator. To retrieve a list of fields, and if they are required or optional, use the **[/operator/{operatorId}/booking-fields](#tag/Operators/paths/~1v1~1operators~1{operator}~1booking-fields/get)** endpoint. Some examples of these fields:
  * `title`: title of the passenger, possible values: `Mr.`, `Ms.`, `Mrs.`, `Miss`.
  * `gender`: gender of the passenger, possible values: `male`, `female`.
  * `date_of_birth`: date of birth of the passenger, format needed: `DD/MM/YYYY`.
  * `email`: the passenger's email address.
  * `bed_preference`: the passenger's bed preference, possible values: `Single Bed`, `Twin Bed`.
  * `nationality`: nationality of the passenger, please use country names from the taxonomy endpoint **[/taxonomy/destinations/country](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1destinations~1{type}/get)**, some examples: `Argentina`, `Austria`, `Bahrain`, `Belgium`, `Australia`. 


#### Accommodation

In the `accommodations` section, it's possible to specify the identifier of an accommodation option, and which passenger numbers should make use of it.

To retrieve a list of accommodation options available for the desired departure, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/departures/{departureId}](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures~1{departureId}/get)** endpoint.

#### Optional extras

The `optional_extras` section works exactly like the `accommodations` section.

To retrieve a list of the optional extra items available for the desired departure, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/departures/{departureId}](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures~1{departureId}/get)** endpoint.

#### Booking conversation page

After the creation of the booking, you will receive in the response a link that leads to the booking conversation page. The link will be available in the `links` object in the response and it will have the type `booking-page`. This page is where all the communication happens between travelers and TourRadar, or the adventure operator. It shows details about the tour booked and has a price breakdown.

An example of a booking conversation page link is:

```json
  "links": [
    {
      "type": "booking-page",
      "url": "https://www.tourradar.com/booking/12345?enquiryCode=fvwffws8hgqqz4blyh13icbyldjqhp6d"
    }
  ],
```

#### Additional information

In the request, it is possible to add these additional fields:

* `partner_booking_code`: the booking code, or reference number, in your system. This will be stored with the booking, and returned with the booking detail request (**[/bookings/{bookingId}](#tag/Bookings/paths/~1v1~1bookings~1{bookingId}/get)** endpoint).
* `store_id`: this is the name or identifier of the store, or agent, that made the booking. It will also be stored and returned.
* `custom_data`: an object containing additional info from your side, stored and retrieved too. Up to 5 string properties can be set in it.

#### Testing payments

In our sandbox environment, you can use one of the Braintree test credit cards. More information about this can be found **[here](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/testing#valid-card-numbers)**.

Please be aware that using one of these valid card numbers does not necessarily mean that the transaction will be successful in the sandbox environment. For example, a transaction with amount between 2000-2999 will cause a payment failure. All the details about transaction amounts and responses can be found **[here](https://developer.paypal.com/braintree/docs/reference/general/testing#transaction-amounts)**.


#### Pending status reason

If there were some errors on the operator side when a booking is created, that booking will have the pending status and the error message received from the operator stored in the field called `status_reason_text`.
Below, you will find an example of this situation:

```json
{
  ...
  "status": "pending",
  "status_reason": "BOOKING_NOT_CONFIRMED",
  "status_reason_text": "Booking could not be confirmed - Missing mandatory fields"
}
```

These fields can be used to understand why there was a problem with the booking and can be leveraged by your CS team to try and make the booking confirmed.

get.description:
This endpoint returns detailed information about a booking, retrieved directly from the operator system.

The call expects two parameters as part of the request path:

- the operator ID
- the booking code (in the operator system)

Additionally, the following query string parameters are supported:

- `currency`: the currency in which the booking was made (use 3-letter ISO 4217 codes, for example `USD` for US Dollars)
- `surname`: the last name of one passenger in the booking
- `next_id`: if the booking has multiple tours, the index of the tour to retrieve

The parameters `currency` and `surname` are required by some operators in order to successfully retrieve a booking.

A full example of a call to this endpoint could be:

```
GET /bookings/operator/406/IVSYDS-A339296?surname=Davis&currency=USD
```

Additional parameters may be added in a future revision, for example the identifier of the agent (store ID) who made the booking.

#### Retrieving operator ID

To retrieve the operator ID for a specific operator, it's possible to use the call [/operators](#tag/Operators/paths/~1v1~1operators/get), which will return a list of all available operators with ID, name, and code.

#### Output definition

The output format is JSON, and the data structure follows closely the OTA standard. In particular, the response is based on the [OTA_TourActivityBookRS.ReservationDetails schema](https://modelviewers.pilotfishtechnology.com/modelviewers/OTA/model/Format.OTA_TourActivityBookRS.ReservationDetails.html).

Unlike OTA, identifiers use the `snake_case` (lowercase, underscore between words) notation, instead of `PascalCase` (first letter of each word capitalized). Furthermore, some fields have been added to the existing schema to support the variety of data returned by operators.

It should be noted that not all operators return all information for bookings. Where possible, data have been structured to minimize the difference between different operators' implementations. The list of fields provided by **all operators** is defined as follows:

| object | field | notes |
| ------ | ----- | ----- |
| confirmation | id | |
| confirmation | status | |
| basic_info | name | Name of the tour/activity |
| basic_info | tour_activity_id | Operator code of the tour/activity |
| schedule | duration | |
| schedule | start | |
| schedule | end | |
| participant_info.individual | given_name | |
| participant_info.individual | surname | |
| participant_info.individual | birth_date | |
| pricing.summary | amount | |
| commission_info | commission_payable_amount | |

> ⚠ **WARNING**: the list is not final in this version

#### Error codes

Every failed request will result in a HTTP status code in the 400 or 500 range. The JSON element `error` in the response will identify the error condition.

This is a list of the possible error codes returned by this API:

| Error code | HTTP Status code | Meaning |
| ------ | ----- | ----- |
| `UNAUTHORIZED` | 401 | Invalid operator credentials |
| `BOOKING_NOT_FOUND` | 404 | Booking not found |
| `OPERATOR_NOT_FOUND` | 412 | Invalid operator ID |
| `INVALID_REQUEST` | 405 | Operation not supported |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | 422 | Parameter missing or invalid |
| `UNKNOWN_ERROR` | 500 | Server failure or unexpected error condition |
| `REQUEST_FAILED` | 502 | Operator server failure |

#### Booking status

The booking status (response field `booking.status`) from different operators is mapped to one of the following values:

- `pending`: the booking has not been confirmed yet
- `confirmed`: the booking has been confirmed
- `declined`: the booking has been cancelled by the operator
- `cancelled`: the booking has been cancelled by the customer or agent

In the event of a status response not recognised by the system, this field will contain `unknown`.
In this case, another response field `booking.operator_status` will contain the original status information provided by the operator.

#### Bookings with multiple tours

Some operators include several tours/activities inside the same booking. In this case, a call to the booking code will return only the first tour/activity (together with their extras, payment information, and so on).

The response, however, will contain an attribute `next_id`, whose value can be added to the query parameters in order to retrieve the next tour/activity in the booking.

The call can be repeated as long as the attribute `next_id` in the response has a value, to get additional components of the booking. When the attribute `next_id` doesn't have a value, the last of the tours/activities in this booking has been reached.

##### Example:

First request:

```
GET /bookings/operator/204/6180043
```

Response:

```
{
    "reservation_details": {
        "basic_info": {
            "name": "4WD Broome to Darwin Overland",
            ....
        }
    },
    "next_id": "1"
}
```

The value `1` for the attribute `next_id` means that there is another component in the same booking, so we can perform the second request:

```
GET /bookings/operator/204/6180043?next_id=1
```

Response:

```
{
    "reservation_details": {
        "basic_info": {
            "name": "Kakadu, Katherine & Litchfield Adventure",
            ....
        }
    }
}
```

This time, the response doesn't contain a `next_id` attribute, which means this booking only has 2 tours/activities in it.

This endpoint returns a list of all destinations in the TourRadar system.

Each destination type can be requested. 

These are the available query parameters:
- `country_id`: filter destinations by country ID. It can be a single integer or a comma-separated list of integers. It is available for all types but country and continent. E.g. `?country_id=1,2,3`

In general, the following attributes will be returned:

- `id`: this is the unique identifier of this destination in the system. The value is immutable, and can be used to setup a mapping between TourRadar destination and the partner's own destinations, or in search requests where a destination ID is needed.
- `name`: the name of the destination.
- `parent_ids`: unique identifiers of this destination's parent destinations. Usually, this will be one value; for example, cities have a state ID as parent, states have a country ID as parent, and so on. There are destination types, for example rivers or national parks, that can belong to more than one country.
- `latitude` and `longitude`: coordinates of the destination. This mostly applies to countries, states, and cities. Other types may not have geographical information.
- `geoname_id`: available for countries and cities, this is the identifier of the destination in the GeoNames geographical database (http://www.geonames.org/). The identifier can be used to facilitate the mapping. *Note*: not 100% of the entries are mapped to a GeoNames entity. TourRadar is committed to constantly improve the data quality, but can't guarantee a perfect match all of the times.
- `country_id`: available for all types but country and continent, this is the identifier of the country the destination belongs to.

In addition, countries have the following additional information:

- `country_code`: two-letter country code in the ISO 3316-1 alpha-2 format.
- `currency_code`: three-letter currency code used in the country in the ISO 4217 format.
- `currency_name`: name of the currency used in the country.
- `electricity_outlets`: an array of one-letter electrical plug types used in the country, as defined by IEC (https://www.iec.ch/world-plugs).

Results will be paginated (1000 elements at a time). If the response contains the `next_page` element, it's possible to access the next 1000 elements by repeating the request with the `page` parameter.

get.description:
Returns a list of tours based on a number of search criteria.

#### Search parameters

The call has a number of optional parameters, that will help you find the perfect tour for your customer.

- `operator`: the ID of the tour operator that operates the tour. Operator IDs can be obtained from the  **[/operators](#tag/Operators/paths/~1v1~1operators/get)** endpoint.
- `currency`: the prices will be returned in the specified currency. Use 3 letter codes, example: `AUD`, `EUR`, `USD`.
- `start_city`: the ID for the start city of the tour. City IDs can be obtained from the **[/taxonomy/destinations/city](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1destinations~1{type}/get)** endpoint.
- `end_city`: the ID for the end city of the tour. City IDs can be obtained from the same endpoint mentioned before.
- `city`: the ID for any city included on the tour itinerary. City IDs can be obtained from the same endpoint mentioned before. Multiple values are allowed, if you are looking for tours that have in itinerary both London and Paris you can make the call `GET /tours/search?city=11149&city=5781`. If you need tours that have in itinerary either London or Paris you can make the call `GET /tours/search?city=11149%2C5781`.
- `country`: the ID for any country included on the tour itinerary. Country IDs can be obtained from the **[/taxonomy/destinations/country](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1destinations~1{type}/get)** endpoint.
- `user_country`: the ID for the country of the passenger's residence. Country IDs can be obtained from the same endpoint mentioned before.
- `primary_country`: the ID for the country in which at least 2/3rd of the tour destinations are located. Country IDs can be obtained from the **[/taxonomy/destinations/country](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1destinations~1{type}/get)** endpoint.
- `continent`: the ID for any continent included on the tour itinerary. Continent IDs can be obtained from the **[/taxonomy/destinations/continent](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1destinations~1{type}/get)** endpoint.
- `natural_destination`: the ID for any natural destination included on the tour itinerary. Natural destination IDs can be obtained from **[/taxonomy/destinations/{type}](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1destinations~1{type}/get)** endpoint (type can be `mountain`, `national_park`, `river`, etc).
- `age`: age range the tour is suitable for, expressed as _min-max_. Using this parameter, all tours that include the desired range will be returned. For example, if `age=18-35`, tours that accepts from 18 to 60 years old will be included in the search result. To only search for an exact age range, use the parameter `exact_age` instead.
- `exact_age`: exact age range the tour is suitable for, expressed as _min-max_ or just _max_. Example: `12-40` meaning the tour is suitable for and accepts 12 to 40 years old passengers.
- `duration`: tour duration in numbers of days, expressed as _min-max_. Example: `5-7` meaning tours between 5 and 7 days of duration.
- `date_range`: range of the desired departure date, expressed as _min-max_. For dates, use the format `YYYYMMDD`, where `YYYY` is the year, `MM` the month, `DD` the day. Example: `20211001-20211030` meaning tours departing in November 2021 (2021-11-01 to 2021-11-30).
- `price`: desired price range for the tour, expressed as _min-max_. Example: `1000-1500` meaning tours between 1000 and 1500 units (in the currency specified by the `currency` parameter).
- `price_per_day`: same as `price`, but using the price per day as value.
- `group_size`: maximum desired group size. Example: `10` will only return tours with a maximum group size of 10 persons.
- `guide_language`: the ID of the language the tour is operated in. Language IDs can be obtained from the **[/taxonomy/languages](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1languages/get)** endpoint.
- `tour_type`: the ID of the tour type you would like to use as a filter. Tour type IDs can be obtained from the **[/taxonomy/tours/types](#tag/Taxonomy/paths/~1v1~1taxonomy~1tours~1types/get)** endpoint. For example, looking at the taxonomy endpoint, the tour type **Sightseeing** has ID 76. If you want to search for tours with this type, the request will look like this: `GET /tours/search?tour_type=76`.
- `is_instant_confirmable`: if true, only tours that can be automatically confirmed will be returned, if false only non instant confirmable.
- `fields`: using this parameter it's possible to restrict the number of fields in the response. Use field names separated by commas. For example, the request `GET /tours/search?fields=tour_id,tour_name,operator` will return just the tour_id, tour_name and operator.

#### Sorting

You can get the results sorted by passing some additional parameters:
- `sort_by`: one of `score`, `price`, or `price_per_day`.
- `sort_order`: `asc` or `desc` for ascending or descending sort order.

The default sort order, if not specified, is by popularity (`score`).


#### Pagination

The search endpoints returns 20 results at a time.

If the response contains the `next_page` element, it's possible to access the next 20 elements by repeating the request with the `page` parameter.

The `limit` parameter can be used to change the number of results per page from the default of 20.

#### Example

A full example of a call to this endpoint could be:

```
GET /tours/search?country=84&tour_type=7&operator=3086&limit=1&page=1
```

Additional parameters may be added in a future revision.

#### Output definition

The list of tours is contained in the `items` array.

The data for each tour will include the ID, the name, images, list of destinations, and categorization.

To retrieve more detailed content about the tour, including itinerary and services, the tour identifier can be used for the **[/tours/{tourId}](#tag/Tours/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}/get)** endpoint.

post.description:
Calculates the price for a booking, given departure date, number and type of passengers, and selected options.

The payload must be sent as a JSON in the request body.
The required entries are:

* `currency`: the currency that will be used for payments.
* `passengers`: the list of passengers in the booking.

Furthermore, it's possible to add the following sections, if needed:

* `accommodations`: defines the desired accommodation types (if the tour offers them), and which passengers will use them.
* `optional_extras`: optional extra items that can be booked together with the tour.

This is an example of how the payload for a price calculation request looks like:

```json
{
  "currency": "EUR",
  "passengers": [
    {
      "pax_number": 1,
      "price_category_id": 1
    },
    {
      "pax_number": 2,
      "price_category_id": 2
    }
  ],
  "accommodations": [
    {
      "id": 345,
      "passengers": [1, 2]
    }
  ],
  "optional_extras": [
    {
      "id": 456,
      "passengers": [2]
    }
  ],
}
```

#### Passengers definition

For each entry in the `passengers` array, these are the required fields:

* `pax_number`: this is the index of the passenger, starting with 1. The passenger number will be used in the accommodation and extras sections of the request, to assign specific passengers to elements of the booking.
* `price_category_id`: this defines the category of the passenger. To retrieve price categories, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/prices](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1prices/get)** endpoint.

#### Accommodation

In the `accommodations` section, it's possible to specify the identifier of an accommodation option, and which passenger numbers should make use of it.

To retrieve a list of accommodation options available for the desired departure, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/departures/{departureId}](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures~1{departureId}/get)** endpoint.

#### Optional extras

The `optional_extras` section works exactly like the `accommodations` section.

To retrieve a list of the optional extra items available for the desired departure, use the **[/tours/{tourId}/departures/{departureId}](#tag/Pricing-and-Availability/paths/~1v1~1tours~1{tourId}~1departures~1{departureId}/get)** endpoint.

#### Response

The response will contain a price breakdown:

  * `price_base`: base price of the tour, also referenced as brochure price.
  * `price_addons`: sum of the mandatory addons that the passenger will have to pay (both upfront and local payments).
  * `price_promotion`: discounted price, it’s equal with price_base – promotion discount.
  * `price_total_upfront`: total price without local payments, it’s equal with price_base – promotion discount + upfront payments. This is the actual price that the customer needs to pay when making a booking.
  * `price_total`: final sale price, it’s equal with price_base – promotion discount + local payments + upfront payments. This contains the price that customer needs to pay and the local payments that will be paid in cash on the tour.
  * `promotion`: details about the promotion applied, if available.
  * `mandatory_addons`: list of the mandatory addons (upfront and local payments). 

Local payments are shared with the customer before making the booking but they are paid only when they reach the destination, in cash.
Upfront payments are mandatory payments made at the time of the booking.

description.example: This is the flagship tour that started it all for Expat Explore! Journey to 8 of Europe's most popular countries. Start off by getting to know the Italian way of life in Rome and the romantic Venice. Explore the gem that is Paris, and meander through the countryside of France. Cross borders to the heart of the Swiss Alps and see castle-lined riverbanks in Germany’s Rhine Valley. Explore the vibrant streets and beautiful canals of Amsterdam. There’s so much in store for you! Please note: there are changes to the itinerary for 2021 departures - see the itinerary and contact us for info
